=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:303-430 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The label_missing hold posts the hold comment and applies ai:blocked from the resolver's earlier refusal without rechecking the issue's current labels or body, so a stale plan run can re-park an issue after a repair and /reclarify.
  WHY: Plan runs have no per-issue concurrency group, so runs can overlap. Severity disagreement: gemini rated it BLOCKER, luna MAJOR, qwen and glm NIT, and minimax gave no severity; the highest is used (BLOCKER mapped to high). sonnet-5_5 explicitly did not carry over this finding.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:307-331 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The comment post and label add are not atomic and have no rollback, so a failed label add leaves the hold comment without ai:blocked.
  WHY: A transient API error or rate limit leaves the issue inconsistent and the job exits with an error without cleaning up the comment.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:307-331 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The `gh api --paginate --slurp` comment fetch is unbounded.
  WHY: A huge comment thread could hit API limits or time out and fail the plan job just to post a hold comment.
- CHANGELOG.md:3418-3432 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The new changelog entry is inserted between the previous entry's main content and its "### For contributors" subsection, splitting them apart.
  WHY: Readers will see the new entry followed by an unrelated "For contributors" section. sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash judged this hunk a stable release fold and not attributable to this PR.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:307-331 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The logic adds `ai:blocked` and writes to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` without checking whether the issue state changed between the resolver refusal and the label/comment write.
  WHY: A stale run can post hold comments and apply `ai:blocked` to a now-valid issue, and plan runs have no per-issue concurrency group.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:307-331 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `ai:blocked` label application and the hold comment creation are not atomic and have no pre-write check that the issue has not been fixed or re-clarified.
  WHY: Concurrent plan runs or a rapid `/reclarify` can lead to duplicate comments and inconsistent state.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:307-331 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The block makes `gh api` and `python3` calls without error handling to revert partial actions if one step fails.
  WHY: If the label add fails, the issue has the hold comment but not `ai:blocked`, and the comment is not cleaned up.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:307-331 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The block makes `gh api --paginate --slurp` calls in an unbounded way.
  WHY: A large comment thread might hit API limits or time out and fail the whole plan job.
- HARDENING: .github/workflows/plan.yml:311-314 | risk_score=2
  PROBLEM: `hold_fail` just exits 1 and does not clean up or log partial state.
  WHY: Suggested fix: wrap it in a trap or log the attempted action before exiting.
- HARDENING: .github/workflows/plan.yml:326-340 | risk_score=3
  PROBLEM: `hold_present` calculation uses an inline `python3` script.
  WHY: Suggested fix: sanitize `hold_comments_file` and check it is non-empty before running python.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:341-430 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The hold executes GitHub writes based only on the resolver refusal from earlier in the same step, without re-reading the live issue state.
  WHY: A concurrent `/reclarify` can race the `hold_present` comment-list read, so the plan hold can post its comment and reapply `ai:blocked` on a fixed issue, and the stale hold marker then blocks a later release.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
